question: Ormsby CHA presidency (Q05/Q89 follow-up)
answer: Hilda Neatby was the CHA's first woman president, in 1962-1963. Margaret A. Ormsby was the second, in 1965-1966. The CHA's own list of presidents shows no woman before Neatby, from L.J. Burpee (1922-1925) onward. The next woman after Ormsby was Margaret E. Prang (1976-1977).

hilda_neatby.presidential_address: Hilda Neatby, "Jean-Olivier Briand: A 'Minor Canadien'," Report of the annual meeting - Canadian Historical Association (1963), 1-18

margaret_ormsby.presidential_address: Margaret A. Ormsby, "A Horizontal View," Historical papers presented at the annual meeting - Canadian Historical Association (1966), 1-13

conflicts_resolved.claim: Ormsby was the 'first woman president' of the CHA
conflicts_resolved.where: Governor General honours record, https://www.gg.ca/en/honours/recipients/146-5300 (as cited in ANSWERS.md Q89; not re-fetched here)
conflicts_resolved.resolution: Contradicted by the CHA's own list. Ormsby was the second woman president. BC Book Look's 'second female president' (https://bcbooklook.com/welcome-to-the-ormsby-review/) agrees with the CHA.

suggested_wording: Margaret Ormsby was president of the Canadian Historical Association in 1965-66, its second woman president after Hilda Neatby (1962-63).
